searchText: May I ask, if ETH2 is very successful, is there any need for other public chains to exist? Or how should other public chains survive? Become a sidechain of ETH? The introduction of sharding to Ethereum, which I suspect is what you are referring to, would enhance Ethereum's throughput but I don't think that predicates other useful chains from existing. At best, it just makes it so you don't *need* another full chain just to have a reasonable amount of throughput. After the success of ETH 2.0, how can other public chains compete with ETH? dot, ada, sol, is there still a need for them in the ETH 2.0 era? There is no ETH 2.0. There is a consensus change upcoming (where we switch to Proof of Stake), and there is the introduction of Sharding, which is further off. In parallel with all of that there is also the state network, state expiry, and maybe zero-knowledge stuff. Ethereum is (intentionally) very general purpose. Just because we have CPUs doesn't mean there is no value in GPUs or ASICs. Specialization can be very valuable. Thank you very much who gets the tips that are received now by the miners after the merge? Priority fee will always go to the block's beneficiary, whoever that may be. Generally, the person who creates the block sets themself as the beneficiary. thank you!
